ticket.title: process-ticket Phase 6: `ci-green` is decided on run-level conclusions alone, so a gating run that never executed the plan's new tests counts as success
ticket.body:
#ai-generated

### Problem

A package reaches `ci-green` and is merged although the tests its own plan promised were never executed by the PR's pipeline. The failure first appears at release time. On 2026-09-20 this burned two version numbers in `Seretos/agent-project-issues` (v0.3.7 and v0.3.8 — neither tag exists) without a single product defect being involved: in both failed release runs `stamp` and `build` succeeded on both OSes.

Phase 6 (`skills/process-ticket/SKILL.md:784-800`) polls `list_pipeline_runs(commit_sha=head)` and posts `ci-green` as soon as every run reports `conclusion == "success"`. `get_pipeline_run(include_failure_excerpt=True)` and `get_pipeline_step_log` are fetched only in the failure branch (`:802-804`). A workflow that never collected the new tests and a workflow that ran them all green are the same JSON to this skill. The three-round exhaustion at `:820` is conclusion-only as well.

Recorded, twice in the same day:

- **#347 / PR #348.** `plan-committed` (comment 5749789815, 12:26:51Z) promised "new `smoke` job in release.yml (windows-latest + ubuntu, both binaries in bin/, runs bash resolution + `wait-pipeline --help`, gates `release`)". `release.yml` is `on: workflow_dispatch` only, so that job could not appear in any pull-request run; run 35512507466 was green. The `ci-green` comment (5749996349, 13:08:13Z) named the gap itself, in prose below the machine block: "The `smoke` job in release.yml has not run yet (it only runs in a release dispatch). Acceptance criterion 1 … is therefore still open for a human." The upper layer reacts to the event name and does not read that text, so the package was merged 18 seconds later. Release run 35514263570 failed 33 minutes after that, in exactly that job, exit 4.
- **#349 / PR #350.** `ci-green` (comment 5750417147, 14:28:48Z): "I also did not open the run's job list to confirm that the four new build/smoke jobs ran, only that the run concluded success." Merged as `62dc3a3`; release run 35522571664 failed 1h55m later, exit 127.

Note the failure shape in both cases: the promised job was **absent** from the gating run, not failing inside it. A check that only looks for red findings does not see this.

Suggested fix (maintainer's choice): on the green path, before posting `ci-green`, verify that what the plan promised — new test files, new jobs, new workflows — actually appears in the gating run for the PR head. If a promised artifact did not execute, treat the round as red and let the existing CI-red repair loop wire it up, inside its existing three-round cap. That needs no new `adev:event` name and no new machine-block field. The deterministic part belongs outside the LLM, in the shape already established by `scripts/critic/stagnation-check.py` (already inside Phase's tool allowance, `SKILL.md:825-830`) and the upper plugin's `scripts/gatekeeper/relation-readback.py`: stdin JSON in, `verdict: ok|gap` out, exit 0/2. A second round of prose telling the same session to check its own bookkeeping is the mechanism that already failed here twice — both comments quoted above *are* that self-check, written honestly and consumed by nobody.

### Acceptance

- A PR whose plan promised a test or CI job that the gating run did not execute does not receive `ci-green`; the session repairs the wiring and re-pushes instead. Demonstrated on a real package run, not asserted in prose.
- The check detects the **absence** of a promised artifact from the run, not only failures within it: replaying the #347 shape — a job added to a `workflow_dispatch`-only workflow while the pull-request run is green — is caught.
- A package whose plan promised nothing new in CI and whose runs are green still reaches `ci-green` without an extra round, and the check itself never consumes a CI round.
- The verdict is produced by a model-free process with its own unit tests, in the shape of `tests/test_release_scripts.py` (this repo) and `tests/test_relation_readback.py` (upper plugin).
- No new `adev:event` name is introduced: the reaction rides the existing `ci-red` path, so `skills/run/SKILL.md` in `agent-ticket-orchestrator` needs no change.

### Prior attempts

None on this symptom. `tests/test_ci_runs_pytest.py` in this repo records an adjacent one: the whole `tests/` suite existed while `lint.yml` ran only jq and a frontmatter check, so "a PR could merge with a failing or entirely broken test suite and CI would stay green throughout" — same failure class, fixed there per-repo rather than at the Phase 6 decision.

Downstream, `Seretos/agent-project-issues` #349 and #351 each added a guard test after a specific failure (`tests/test_351_workflow_checkout_guard.py` parametrises over every job of every workflow file). Those guards are per-repo and per-incident and do not generalise to packages in other projects, which is why this ticket targets the decision point instead.

A companion ticket covering the other direction — an acceptance criterion that announces the need for a new pipeline capability *before* dispatch, so the capability becomes its own dependency package — is filed in `Seretos/agent-ticket-orchestrator`.

**Blocked: the premise the gatekeeper asked to verify is false, and the substitute is a design decision.**

Planner finding, quoted verbatim:

> PREMISE FALSIFIED: "per-job data for a green run (names of the jobs that actually executed) is obtainable through the tools Phase 6 is allowed", checked via reading the MCP/CLI implementations (`project_issues_plugin/cli.py`, `tools/pipelines.py`, `lib_python_projects/providers/github.py`), found: a green run exposes **no job list at all**.

What each tool returns:
- `wait-pipeline` stdout is `{state, waited_s, runs:[{id, event, status, conclusion, url}]}`, with no jobs.
- `get_pipeline_run` attaches `failing_jobs[]` only when `conclusion == "failure"`.
- `get_pipeline_step_log` needs a `job_id` that only that failure block yields.
- `list_pipeline_runs` works at workflow level only.

What is obtainable: run presence per workflow file. `list_pipeline_runs(project_id, commit_sha=<head>, workflow="<file>.yml")` is scoped server-side to that workflow.

**Question: which substitute for per-job data should the check use?**

**(a) Diff-derived static reachability plus per-workflow run presence (recommended).**
- The check finds jobs the branch diff adds to a workflow file.
- It flags a gap if that workflow cannot fire on this PR, i.e. it is `workflow_dispatch`/`schedule`-only or `push` with a non-matching `branches:` filter.
- It also flags a gap if that workflow has no successful run for the head.
- This decides both recorded incidents (#347 and #349) with no upstream change.
- Cost: a job that sits in a workflow which does run but is skipped by an `if:` condition is not caught.
- Implementation: model-free `scripts/ci-promised-check.py` (stdin JSON, `verdict: ok|gap`, exit 0/2), consulted on both `ci-green` lanes of Phase 6. A gap posts `ci-red` and enters the existing repair loop. No new event, no new machine-block field.

**(b) Block on an upstream capability first.**
- File a dependency package on `agent-project-issues` to expose a job list for any run, then check real execution.
- Cost: this ticket stalls behind another repo's release, and the burned-version-number failure can recur in the meantime.

**(c) Planner-declared promised-artifacts section instead of the diff.**
- `agents/planner.md` gains a machine-readable block that the check reads.
- Cost: a declaration can be forgotten. On #347 the prose promise existed and the wiring failed, so this reintroduces the self-check failure mode the ticket is about.

**Recommendation: (a).** Reply on this ticket with the chosen option and the run continues from planning.

**What I checked:**
- The ticket, the gatekeeper's Frame comment, `AGENTS.md` and `SKILL.md`.
- The `agent-project-issues` CLI/MCP implementation. This was the planner's check, not mine.

The premise check settles the tool-data question. The choice of substitute is a scope and design trade-off (upstream dependency vs. a static heuristic with a known blind spot), and the ticket does not settle it.

A full draft plan for (a) is at `.adev/122-1/plan.md` in the worktree, so choosing (a) costs no rework. No code was written. The branch has no commits of its own and nothing to push.

#ai-generated

## Blocked triage (run)

**Question:** which substitute for per-job data should the Phase 6 check use, given that a green run exposes no job list?

**Chosen option: (a)** — diff-derived static reachability plus per-workflow run presence, implemented as a model-free `scripts/ci-promised-check.py` (stdin JSON, `verdict: ok|gap`, exit 0/2), consulted on both `ci-green` lanes of Phase 6. A gap posts `ci-red` and enters the existing repair loop. No new event, no new machine-block field.

**Reasoning (all from this ticket):**
- The ticket's Problem section rejects (c) by name: a self-declared bookkeeping step is the mechanism that already failed twice.
- The Prior-attempts section moves (b), the upstream job-list capability, into a separate companion ticket in `agent-ticket-orchestrator`. It is not an open choice here, and it satisfies none of this ticket's acceptance criteria on its own.
- The maintainer's "Suggested fix" paragraph prescribes (a)'s exact shape. Detecting the absence of a promised artifact, being model-free and unit-tested, adding no new event, and staying silent when the diff adds no CI jobs are all met by (a).
- The named cost of (a), a job skipped by an `if:` inside a workflow that does run, is outside the acceptance criteria.

**Note for the planner:** Phase 6 may only run scripts named in the SKILL.md Hard-rules allowlist. The new script must be added there, the same way `tests/test_pipeline_contract.py::test_stagnation_check_is_in_the_skills_own_bash_allowlist` pins `stagnation-check.py`. The draft plan for (a) at `.adev/122-1/plan.md` can be reused.
